explanation: The theorem is a fact about the library's own table `g2Length := ![1, 3, 1, 1, 3, 3, 1, 3, 1, 1, 3, 3]` on `Fin 12`: shifting the index by 6 returns the same entry. The proof just checks all twelve cases with `decide`. All of the content comes from this explicit definition, and Mathlib has no declaration about this table. Mathlib's root-system API does have general results saying a root and its negative have the same length under an invariant form. But this is a numeric table indexed by `Fin 12`, so none of those results gives the statement in one or two lines. I did not search further, because the statement only concerns the library's own definition.
